items.title: Planetary boundaries
items.claim: The 2023 update to the planetary boundaries framework (Richardson et al.) found how many of the nine boundaries had been transgressed?
items.reveal_title: Six boundaries transgressed in the 2023 assessment
items.reveal:
Richardson et al. (2023, Science Advances) reported climate change, biosphere integrity, biogeochemical flows, land-system change, freshwater change and novel entities all outside the proposed safe operating space.

Ozone, ocean acidification and atmospheric aerosol loading remained within their limits.
items.why: Environmental science increasingly operates with multi-dimensional dashboards rather than a single climate metric.

items.title: Yellowstone wolves: the headline vs the evidence
items.claim: Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995. The story of dramatic 'rivers changing course' from a trophic cascade has been widely shared. What does subsequent research say?

options.text: The full headline cascade is well supported in all sites
Effects on elk, willows and beavers are real but more localised and partial than the viral story implies

items.reveal_title: Real effects, less dramatic than the viral version
items.reveal:
Marshall et al. (2013) and later work found vegetation responses were patchy and depended on hydrology and other carnivores. The strongest behavioural-cascade claims have been challenged.

The ecological story remains genuinely interesting; the simplified version travels further than the nuanced one.
items.why: Popular ecological narratives often outrun the evidence even when the underlying science is robust.

items.title: Paris Agreement targets
items.claim: The Paris Agreement (2015) commits parties to holding warming below 2 C and pursuing efforts to limit it to what?
items.reveal:
Article 2 of the Paris Agreement specifies 'well below 2 C' and 'pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 C'. IPCC's 2018 SR15 report assessed the 1.5 C pathway in detail.

In 2023 the global mean temperature anomaly briefly exceeded 1.5 C above pre-industrial.
items.why: Climate policy numbers carry technical meaning beyond their headline use.
